title: Tenant override cache invalidation caused hosted routing of private requests
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customer escalation: a subset of requests from VPC/private tenants were routed to hosted model endpoints for ~2 hours due to a cache invalidation race between tenant-scoped override and global policy refresh. The misroute exposed the possibility of tenant model choice and region preference leaking into hosted pools and increased token costs for affected customers. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigation, root cause, fix, and follow-ups.
impact: High - three enterprise customers reported increased costs and one reported a potential data isolation concern (no confirmed data egress), peak error rate increased 8% for affected tenants, latency spikes, and SLA breach risk during incident window.
customer_reports: CustA (finance, EU): reported sudden spike in token usage and returned model mismatch vs pinned private model
CustB (healthcare, US-East): reported higher latency and flagged security team about unexpected endpoint hostnames
CustC (SaaS, global): automated alerts for model-version drift triggered
repro_steps: 1) Configure tenant with private deployment and tenant-scoped routing override pointing to private model variant
2) Trigger concurrent policy refresh: push global catalog update while tenant policies are reloaded
3) Rapidly send requests during overlap window; observe routing table entry momentarily pointing to hosted pool due to stale cache read
4) Confirm via routing logs: request_id -> route mapping shows HOSTED:<model> while tenant metadata indicates PRIVATE:<pinned-model>
timeline_summary: 2026-03-01 09:12 UTC - First customer alert (CustA) via support with spike in usage
2026-03-01 09:30 UTC - Oncall routed to routing/infra team; initial mitigation: added emergency rule to pin affected tenant to fallback private pool
2026-03-01 10:05 UTC - Engineering identified correlation with policy refresh job at 09:11 UTC
2026-03-01 10:40 UTC - Hotfix deployed to ensure atomic cache swap semantics (routing-2.7.1) ; monitored for next 2 hours

mitigation: Emergency pin applied for impacted tenants in control plane to force routing to private pool; increased logging and sampling for routing decisions; temporarily slowed policy refresh cadence while fix was developed.
root_cause: Race condition in cache invalidation: tenant-scoped override entries were stored in the local routing cache with a TTL and a two-step refresh (delete then repopulate). During concurrent global catalog refresh, a cache read occurred after delete and before repopulate, which fell back to a global resolution that favored hosted pools. The resolver did not treat tenant-scoped entries as strongly authoritative during 'empty' cache reads.
fix_summary: Implemented atomic cache swap for tenant-scoped overrides (swap new map into place instead of delete/populate) and strengthened resolver precedence so that empty local-key reads consult a persistent override table before falling back. Added unit + integration tests and a canary rollout to dedicated/private infra before full deployment.
monitoring_changes: Added routing decision traces for tenant overrides (sample=100%)
New alert: tenant-routing-fallback-rate > 0.5% over 5m for high-tier tenants
Dashboard: Tenant routing breakdown by resolved pool (hosted/dedicated/private) added to Console -> Observability -> Routing
postmortem_notes: Customer communication: sent detailed timeline and mitigation summary to affected customers; offered credits for overage and follow-up security review for CustB

Process change: policy refresh job will now acquire a short-lived global 'policy-lock' and perform atomic map replacement; rollout gating for future routing changes requires canary across private and dedicated pools
Testing: added multi-tenant simultaneous policy refresh test to CI that simulates delete/repopulate race under load
